thread.title: Alphabet (GOOGL) 3rd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Alphabet (GOOGL) 3rd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect
text:
Shutterstock photo
I asked recently whether there was any merit to the so-called "Octoberphobia." Specifically, I came to believe the idea that stocks would decline in October just because that’s what they’ve done historically seemed ludicrous to me.
Well, here we are. So far this month, the S&P 500 is down about 7%, while the Nasdaq Composite is down almost 9%. Among the decliners is Google parent Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), which is set to report third quarter fiscal 2018 earnings results Thursday after the closing bell. The tech conglomerate has seen its shares fall 7% this month and 14% since the start of the quarter.
The decline in Google, as well as that of FAANG stocks (down 9% this month collectively) invites the question whether the FAANG trade has peaked? I don’t believe it has, especially given the rate at which their revenue and earnings are rising. For Google, however, there’s also some concern among investors that the company may face stricter government intervention as official press for more security and privacy of consumers’ data.
The question is, to what extent will these events impact company’s earnings results? My guess is it won’t. Strong top and bottom line Q3 growth is what investors should expect. Past concerns about the company’s profit margins have been an afterthought given that it now has a much strong grip on Traffic Acquisition Costs in the advertising business, among other operational improvements.
In the period that ended September, Wall Street is looking for the Mountain View, Calif.-based tech giant earn $10.43 per share on revenue of $34.04 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to $9.57 per share on revenue of $27.77 billion. For the full year, ending in December, earnings of $39.81 per share would rise 23% year over year, while full-year revenue of the $137.06 billion would rise 23.6% year over year.
In the second quarter, Google delivered total revenues of $32.65 billion, which surge 26% year over year. Just as impressive, the company accounted for roughly 40% of the total U.S. digital advertising market, according to eMarketer. This compares to a 20% claim for Facebook ( FB ). But that duopoly must now contend with Amazon, which has announced its presence in the digital advertising realm with authority .
On Thursday Wall Street will want to see that Google can still maintain a stranglehold of its lifeblood. In the second quarter, its advertising revenues surged roughly 24% from $22.672 billion to reach $28.087 billion. Analysts expects third quarter ad revenues to rise about 21% to just under $30 billion. This compares to just north of $24 billion in the year-ago quarter.
Elsewhere, Wall Street will be interested in the company’s next-generation Pixel 3 and the Pixel 3XL smartphones, launched recently. Will these devices be enough to take a bite out of Apple’s ( AAPL ) iPhone dominance? Will its Google Home Hub be enough to fight Amazon’s Alexa — the leader in the crowded home assistant market? And to say nothing about the company’s Other Bets segments, which focuses on areas such as self-driving cars and artificial intelligence.
All told, there are tons of questions that will be answered upon the earnings release and during the conference call with analysts that follows.
